from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window", [
            "Think of filters as sliding magnifying glasses.",
            "Scanning photographs extracts vital visual details.",
            "Imagine our filter detecting cat ears."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        grid = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.1) for _ in range(9)]).arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0.2)
        highlight = Square(side_length=0.3, color=YELLOW).move_to(grid[4])
        filter_box = Square(side_length=1.0, color=BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(highlight))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(filter_box, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(filter_box))
        # Move filter box over the grid
        self.play(filter_box.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.8), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(filter_box.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.8), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(filter_box.animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Indicate(filter_box))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Convolution combines input and kernel matrices.",
            "Multiply overlapping elements, then sum them up.",
            "Flipping the kernel defines the operation formally.",
            "Slide across grid to create new map.",
            "One input pixel results from every shift."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Core: Element-wise Product and Sum", lecture_lines)

        # Assets
        vec_a = MathTex("A = [1, 2, 3]", color=BLUE)
        vec_k = MathTex("K = [0.5, 1, 2]", color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_a, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_k, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(vec_a), Write(vec_k))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Showing product elements
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(vec_a[0][i+2].get_center() + DOWN*0.5) for i in range(3)])
        # Actually, let's just use arrows for simplicity
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(vec_a[0][i+2].get_bottom(), vec_k[0][i+2].get_top(), color=WHITE, buff=0.1) for i in range(3)])
        self.play(Create(arrows))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        # Just highlighting kernel
        self.play(Indicate(vec_k))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        # Visual slide simulation
        rect = Square(side_length=0.5, color=GREEN).next_to(vec_a, RIGHT)
        self.play(FadeIn(rect))
        self.play(rect.animate.shift(RIGHT))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        res = MathTex("= 0.5 + 2 + 6 = 8.5", color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(res, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(res))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dot products measure how well patterns match.",
            "High values indicate strong pattern alignment.",
            "Convolution acts as a powerful feature detector."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Sync: Dot Products", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        v1 = Vector([1, 2], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([2, 1], color=WHITE)
        label_dot = MathTex(r"a \cdot b = \sum a_i b_i", color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(v1, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(v2, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(label_dot, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(label_dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        highlight = label_dot.copy().set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(label_dot.copy(), highlight))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Image Processing & CNNs", [
            "Convolutional layers stack to form deep networks.",
            "Simple edges evolve into complex object recognition.",
            "Drones use convolutions to identify landing pads."
        ])
        
        # Create a grid for the filter visualization
        grid_rows, grid_cols = 5, 5
        image_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.7) for _ in range(grid_rows * grid_cols)])
        image_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=grid_rows, cols=grid_cols, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(image_grid, 'A1', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(image_grid)

        # Create filter
        filter_box = Square(side_length=0.7, color=YELLOW)
        filter_box.scale(0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_box, 'A1', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.add(filter_box)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        # Animate filter sliding
        path = VGroup(*[image_grid[i] for i in [0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14]])
        self.play(filter_box.animate.move_to(image_grid[2].get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(filter_box.animate.move_to(image_grid[12].get_center()), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        feature_cell = image_grid[6].copy().set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(feature_cell))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Reflection", [
            "Convolution is scanning, multiplying, and summing.",
            "It serves as a template matching engine.",
            "Visualize it extracting features from data."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        title_obj = Text("Convolution", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("Sliding Window", font_size=32, color="#FFCC00")
        label2 = Text("Dot Product", font_size=32, color="#00FFCC")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(title_obj, "B3")
        self.play(FadeIn(title_obj))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFCC00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D5")
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(label1), GrowFromCenter(label2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFCC")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        pulse_group = VGroup(title_obj, label1, label2)
        self.play(
            pulse_group.animate.scale(1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            pulse_group.animate.scale(1/1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF99FF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Understanding Discrete Convolutions: From Filters to Features
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Engineering Students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a 'filter' moving over data. Use an analogy of a magnifying glass scanning a photograph to extract specific details like edges or brightness.
sections.example: A 3x3 'cat-ear detector' filter sliding over a pixel grid of a house pet image to highlight where the ears are located.

sections.title: Mathematical Core: Element-wise Product and Sum
sections.content: Define discrete convolution as the sum of element-wise products. Visually represent this as two overlapping matrices: the input matrix (A) and the kernel (K). Emphasize the 'flip and shift' mechanism (flipping the kernel) for formal definition.
sections.example: Visual animation of a 3x3 kernel sliding over a 5x5 grid, showing the multiplication of overlapping values and the summation resulting in a single output pixel.

sections.title: Prerequisite Sync: Dot Products
sections.content: Briefly recap the Dot Product: the idea that the result is high only when the kernel 'matches' the underlying pattern. This ensures students understand why convolution functions as a 'feature detector'.
sections.example: Comparing a 'vertical edge' kernel to a vertical line on a image grid—demonstrating how the high multiplication values produce a bright spot in the output.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Image Processing & CNNs
sections.content: Transition to modern applications. Explain how stacks of convolutions form Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Move from simple edge detection to complex object recognition.
sections.example: A drone navigation system using a convolution layer to identify a 'landing pad' symbol on the ground amidst a noisy background.

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Recap: Convolution = Scanning + Dot Product + Feature Extraction. Encourage learners to visualize convolution as a 'template matching' engine.
sections.example: A quick visual recap of the 'cat ear' filter evolving into a complex 'cat face' detector in deep layers.
